chapter: New Orleans second line and Armstrong
title: Church, camp meetings, gangs, and first sight of young Armstrong
summary: Jackson discusses Williams Chapel, Methodists and Catholics, camp meeting music, second-line gangs, and first seeing Armstrong at the Jones home playground.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Well did you hear any music in the churches much? Your mother, which church did she sing?
Well it was Williams Chapel, that's where I was Christian. I was Christian at Williams Chapel up there, I think it was up on Cherokee Street. Williams Chapel.
Methodist. Methodist. Some of them was Catholic and some of them were like the Marchion and the French one.
But you don't remember hearing many spirituals or gospel music in the church you think when

you were up there? I heard them at camp meetings. I threw in one of the same park as a camp meeting, I always remember, yeah. And it's just like I heard Mahalia Jackson last night. I mean that music's got a swing to it. When that piano starts to kind of vamp and then you know give it an intro, it's a swing there. And I've been hearing that all my life. It's a swing there. Now about those Methodists and the Catholics and the Protestants, a boy named Chigar, I was raised up. His name was, I think his name was Initial Jewels. And I used to go to the Catholic Church there on Faurant and Napoleon Avenue. I used to go. I mean that's the only church in the Orange that the both races did in the mixing. I mean I can go way back then. And the Catholics always seemed to be better to color than the other people. Because I went to the church several times, you know, and we sat where we weren't sitting and there wasn't nobody saying anything to him. It's not great a day. But it's probably that way of the day. Now this Chigar and his brother, we called him Tutu, Chigar's name was Initial Jewels, the Creole people. And so, but getting back to the Catholic, now the Elick Marchand, Joe Marchand, my cousin, they were strictly Catholic people. And the Francois was Catholic people. Then the Mauritius, the Methodists. So I was a Christian Methodist. And it's been that way ever since. So at Second Line, every kid of any size, if there's people who are not watching, you join that parade, and you're just marching and marching and you find yourself in another part of town. And when you get in the sides, them gangs, they run you, they get behind you and run you back where you come from. They'd ask you for a nickel or something, if you didn't give it to them they'd hit you or anything like that. They had them gangs they used to fight. But they wasn't like these gangs now, you know, they wasn't the guns and things. These kids now are killing one another. They hit you with your fists or maybe throw bricks at you or something like that. But the first time I saw a lawyer I never will forget. I wish you could have saw him, Bill. He just stood up there in front of the rest of the boys. The Joneses home, baby. Yeah, with a sticker just like this, a picture just like this. If you ever saw the picture, that's the way he was. He was destined to be great, Bill. He was destined to be great. You could see it in and in. And he couldn't have been over about twelve years old at the best. Because he was back there with another boy from the old named Gus. And I know some other boys played with him back there. You ever have George Washington strombone playing with him? Yeah, sure. He played with Buddy T. P.T. and then. Well George and a fellow called Frazier played bass horn. He played back there with Lewis. Gus, George and Frazier, they played back there. And they used to play this Maryland, well that's the tune they play, that's one of the tunes they play, that Tonlefong playground. At the first time I saw Lewis, and I told Lewis about it, I said you know, I saw you, but I didn't know who you was, that's who he was. And we came up here, we made friends, I'll never forget that first night he hit Chicago. And then he and Liv fell in love and we got married.
How was the hat was it, you said he had on a sailor hat or something?
He had on one of these sailors, you know straw hats? Oh, I know. With a brown backsuit. Yeah. Yeah.
Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
